ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a DC circuit. On the left there is a power supply labeled 5V. Beside the power supply symbol it is indicated that the upper terminal is “−” and the lower terminal is “+”. There is a switch S at the top, and the current drawing shows the switch open; the upper left node is labeled a, and the upper right node is labeled b. The right branch has a 5Ω resistor, connected to the lower wire and returning to the bottom common node. Reasoning: Take the bottom wire as 0 V. Since switch S is open, the right-side 5Ω resistor branch does not form a closed loop, so the current is 0 and the voltage drop across the resistor is 0. Therefore the potential at point b is equal to the potential of the bottom wire, namely V_b = 0 V. In the figure, the lower terminal of the power supply is positive and the upper terminal is negative, and the power supply voltage is 5V, so point a connected to the upper terminal of the power supply is 5V lower than the bottom wire, namely V_a = -5 V. Thus U_ab = V_a - V_b = -5 V - 0 V = -5 V.

raw_record.question_text: In the DC circuit shown in the figure, when the switch S is in the off position, what is the voltage \(U_{ab}\) between terminals a and b?

method.method_draft: Take the bottom rail as 0 V. Because S is off, no current flows through the right-side 5Ω resistor, so its voltage drop is 0 and V_b equals the bottom rail, 0 V. The source polarity in the image shows the lower terminal is + and the upper terminal is −, so the upper source node connected to a is 5 V below the bottom rail: V_a = -5 V. Therefore U_ab = V_a - V_b = -5 V.

method.method_draft: Interpret U_ab as the open-circuit voltage from a to b after the switch is opened. On the right side, b is tied to the lower conductor through the 5Ω resistor but carries no current, so b is at the same potential as the lower conductor. On the left side, the 5 V source places its upper terminal, which is terminal a, 5 V lower than the lower conductor because the plus sign is at the bottom. Thus terminal a is 5 V below terminal b, giving U_ab = -5 V.
